01-01.text: Cyprus and Malta officially adopt the euro as their currency.

01-02.text: Crude oil prices hit 100 dollars per barrel for the first time in trading history.

01-03.text: Barack Obama wins the Iowa Democratic caucuses, launching his campaign into national prominence.

01-04.text: The 2008 Dakar Rally is cancelled due to security concerns in Mauritania.

01-05.text: This week in 2008, the Hollywood writers strike halts production on dozens of popular television series.

01-06.text: Bill Gates delivers his final Consumer Electronics Show keynote address before stepping down from Microsoft.

01-07.text: This week in 2008, Warner Bros. announces it will release films only on Blu-ray, a heavy blow to HD DVD.

01-08.text: Hillary Clinton wins the New Hampshire Democratic primary, staging an unexpected political comeback.

01-09.text: Astronomers detect supernova SN 2008D in galaxy NGC 2770 using NASA's Swift satellite.

01-10.text: Tata Motors unveils the Tata Nano in New Delhi, marketed as the world's cheapest production car.

01-11.text: This week in 2008, tech companies showcase early ultra-thin OLED display prototypes at CES in Las Vegas.

01-12.text: This week in 2008, NASA prepares the MESSENGER spacecraft for humanity's first Mercury flyby in thirty years.

01-13.text: The 65th Golden Globe Awards ceremony is replaced by a brief press conference due to the Hollywood writers strike.

01-14.text: NASA's MESSENGER spacecraft completes its first flyby of Mercury, photographing previously unseen terrain.

01-15.text: Steve Jobs unveils the ultra-thin MacBook Air at Macworld, famously pulling it from a manila envelope.

01-16.text: This week in 2008, Apple announces Time Capsule, a wireless backup drive built into an AirPort Extreme base station.

01-17.text: World chess champion Bobby Fischer passes away in Reykjavik at the age of 64.

01-18.text: The found-footage monster movie Cloverfield opens in theaters after a viral marketing campaign.

01-19.text: This week in 2008, the HD DVD Promotional Group cancels its promotional events following major studio defections.

01-20.text: The television drama Breaking Bad premieres on AMC.

01-21.text: Global stock markets suffer sharp declines amid growing fears of a United States economic recession.

01-22.text: Criterion Games releases Burnout Paradise, introducing open-world racing to the franchise.

01-23.text: This week in 2008, fans of Cloverfield keep digging through its viral websites for hidden clues.

01-24.text: Societe Generale reveals that unauthorized trades by Jerome Kerviel caused billions in losses.

01-25.text: Severe winter storms strike central and southern China, disrupting power grids and transportation.

01-26.text: Maria Sharapova wins the women's singles title at the Australian Open without dropping a set.

01-27.text: Novak Djokovic wins his first Grand Slam singles title, defeating Jo-Wilfried Tsonga at the Australian Open.

01-28.text: This week in 2008, hype peaks in Japan for Super Smash Bros. Brawl, due out at the end of the month.

01-29.text: Asteroid 2007 TU24 passes safely by Earth at about 1.4 times the distance to the Moon.

01-30.text: Severed undersea cables in the Mediterranean Sea disrupt up to 70 percent of internet traffic in Egypt and India.

01-31.text: Nintendo releases Super Smash Bros. Brawl for the Wii in Japan, introducing third-party icons Snake and Sonic.

02-01.text: Microsoft bids 44.6 billion dollars to acquire Yahoo!, initiating a fierce months-long tech battle.

02-02.text: French President Nicolas Sarkozy marries singer and former model Carla Bruni in Paris.

02-03.text: The New York Giants defeat the undefeated New England Patriots 17-14 to win Super Bowl XLII.

02-04.text: NASA beams the Beatles song "Across the Universe" into deep space to celebrate the agency's 50th anniversary.

02-05.text: Twenty-four US states hold primary elections on Super Tuesday, the largest single-day voting event in primary history.

02-06.text: Hollywood studios and the Writers Guild of America reach a tentative agreement to end their three-month strike.

02-07.text: Space Shuttle Atlantis launches on mission STS-122, delivering the Columbus research module to the ISS.

02-08.text: Capcom releases Devil May Cry 4 in Europe, bringing the hack-and-slash series to the PS3 and Xbox 360.

02-09.text: Space Shuttle Atlantis docks with the International Space Station to install the European Columbus module.

02-10.text: Amy Winehouse wins five Grammy Awards, including Record of the Year and Song of the Year for "Rehab".

02-11.text: Astronauts successfully attach the European Columbus laboratory module to the International Space Station.

02-12.text: The Writers Guild of America officially ends its 100-day strike after members vote to approve a new contract.

02-13.text: Australian Prime Minister Kevin Rudd issues a formal apology to the country's Indigenous peoples and the Stolen Generations.

02-14.text: This week in 2008, major retailers begin pulling HD DVD stock, signaling victory for the Blu-ray format.

02-15.text: Walmart announces it will exclusively carry Blu-ray movies and players, effectively ending the high-def disc war.

02-16.text: Japanese public broadcaster NHK reports that Toshiba is preparing to abandon its HD DVD format.

02-17.text: Kosovo's parliament declares independence from Serbia during an extraordinary session in Pristina.

02-18.text: The British government takes Northern Rock into public ownership, the first major UK bank nationalization in decades.

02-19.text: Toshiba officially concedes the high-definition format war, announcing it will discontinue HD DVD players and discs.

02-20.text: A US Navy missile cruiser shoots down the malfunctioning military reconnaissance satellite USA-193 in orbit.

02-21.text: A total lunar eclipse turns the Moon deep red, visible across the Americas, Europe, and Africa.

02-22.text: This week in 2008, Sony celebrates Blu-ray's market victory as retailers worldwide phase out rival format HD DVD.

02-23.text: A B-2 Spirit stealth bomber crashes during takeoff in Guam; both pilots safely eject, marking the aircraft's first loss.
02-23.src: 2008 Andersen Air Force Base B-2 accident

02-24.text: No Country for Old Men wins Best Picture and Best Director at the 80th Academy Awards in Hollywood.

02-25.text: Lee Myung-bak is inaugurated as President of South Korea, promising economic revitalization and closer ties with the US.

02-26.text: The Svalbard Global Seed Vault officially opens in Norway, safeguarding millions of crop seeds deep inside an Arctic mountain.

02-27.text: The European Commission slaps Microsoft with a record 899 million euro fine for failing to comply with antitrust orders.

02-28.text: Apple sends invitations for a special event in March to unveil third-party software development for the iPhone.

02-29.text: Mistwalker and Hironobu Sakaguchi release the acclaimed JRPG Lost Odyssey for the Xbox 360 in Europe.

03-01.text: The Andean diplomatic crisis begins after Colombian forces carry out a cross-border raid against FARC rebels in Ecuador.

03-02.text: Dmitry Medvedev wins the Russian presidential election, succeeding Vladimir Putin.

03-03.text: This week in 2008, excitement mounts across North America ahead of the release of Super Smash Bros. Brawl.

03-04.text: Brett Favre announces his retirement from the NFL after sixteen seasons with the Green Bay Packers.

03-05.text: This week in 2008, Apple prepares to announce the iPhone Software Development Kit at a special media event.

03-06.text: Apple announces the iPhone SDK and plans for the App Store, enabling third-party native apps on iPhone.

03-07.text: This week in 2008, software developers gain access to the first beta version of Apple's iPhone SDK.

03-08.text: This week in 2008, movie trailers for Marvel's Iron Man circulate widely, building massive summer anticipation.

03-09.text: Nintendo releases Super Smash Bros. Brawl in North America for the Wii, setting rapid sales records.

03-10.text: The European Space Agency's first Jules Verne cargo spacecraft begins orbital maneuvers en route to the ISS.

03-11.text: Space Shuttle Endeavour launches on mission STS-123 to deliver Japan's Kibo laboratory module to the ISS.

03-12.text: Hulu officially launches its ad-supported online video streaming service to the public in the United States.

03-13.text: Gold prices surpass 1,000 dollars per ounce for the first time in history on the New York Mercantile Exchange.

03-14.text: The Federal Reserve provides an emergency bailout loan to Bear Stearns to avert an immediate collapse.

03-15.text: This week in 2008, Wall Street faces immense uncertainty as Bear Stearns teeters on the brink of failure.

03-16.text: JPMorgan Chase agrees to acquire struggling investment bank Bear Stearns for two dollars per share.

03-17.text: Astronauts assemble the two-armed robotic system Dextre during a spacewalk on the International Space Station.

03-18.text: The US Federal Reserve cuts its benchmark interest rate by 75 basis points to stem mounting financial turmoil.

03-19.text: Astronomers detect gamma-ray burst GRB 080319B, the most distant object ever visible to the naked human eye.

03-20.text: This week in 2008, developers experiment with the newly released beta of Microsoft Internet Explorer 8.

03-21.text: This week in 2008, physicists at CERN prepare the Large Hadron Collider for its scheduled debut later in the year.

03-22.text: Ma Ying-jeou is elected President of Taiwan, pledging closer economic relations with mainland China.

03-23.text: This week in 2008, gaming magazines showcase exclusive preview coverage for the upcoming Grand Theft Auto IV.

03-24.text: The Olympic flame is lit in Olympia, Greece, marking the start of the global torch relay for the 2008 Beijing Games.

03-25.text: Sony releases PS3 firmware update 2.20, adding BD-Live interactive features and Blu-ray Profile 2.0 support.

03-26.text: Space Shuttle Endeavour lands safely at Kennedy Space Center, concluding a 16-day mission to assemble the ISS.

03-27.text: This week in 2008, gamers celebrate the European release of Gran Turismo 5 Prologue on the PlayStation 3.

03-28.text: Polyphony Digital releases Gran Turismo 5 Prologue in Europe, showcasing photorealistic graphics on PlayStation 3.

03-29.text: Cities across the globe switch off non-essential lights for one hour during the international Earth Hour event.

03-30.text: The Open Skies Agreement between the European Union and the United States officially takes effect.

03-31.text: This week in 2008, Rockstar Games releases the third official trailer for Grand Theft Auto IV, fueling viral hype.

04-01.text: Google and Virgin Group announce 'Project Virgle', an elaborate April Fools' prank proposing a settlement on Mars.

04-02.text: The 20th NATO summit convenes in Bucharest to discuss missile defense systems and alliance expansion.

04-03.text: The European Space Agency's Jules Verne cargo spacecraft completes its first automated docking with the ISS.

04-04.text: Beyoncé and Jay-Z marry in an intimate, private ceremony in New York City.

04-05.text: This week in 2008, excitement mounts globally ahead of the upcoming theatrical release of Marvel's Iron Man.

04-06.text: Protests disrupt the Olympic torch relay through London ahead of the Beijing 2008 Olympic Games.

04-07.text: Officials extinguish the Olympic torch several times during the relay through Paris amid demonstrations.

04-08.text: Soyuz TMA-12 launches, carrying Yi So-yeon into orbit as South Korea's first astronaut.

04-09.text: Officials secretly reroute the Olympic torch relay in San Francisco to avoid large protests.

04-10.text: Nepal holds a historic Constituent Assembly election, leading to the end of its 240-year-old monarchy.

04-11.text: This week in 2008, Rockstar Games releases the official gameplay trailer for Grand Theft Auto IV.

04-12.text: This week in 2008, developers build early prototypes using Apple's new iPhone Software Development Kit.

04-13.text: Trevor Immelman wins the 2008 Masters Tournament at Augusta National, earning his first major title.

04-14.text: Marvel Studios hosts the world premiere of Iron Man in Sydney, Australia, kicking off the MCU.

04-15.text: Pope Benedict XVI arrives in Washington, D.C., beginning his first apostolic visit to the United States.
04-15.src: Pope Benedict XVI's visit to the United States

04-16.text: This week in 2008, retail stores worldwide prepare midnight launch events for Grand Theft Auto IV.

04-17.text: This week in 2008, Intel's new low-power Atom processor gets ready to power a wave of cheap netbooks.

04-18.text: This week in 2008, Nintendo announces that global sales of the Wii console have reached landmark figures.

04-19.text: Soyuz TMA-11 lands safely in Kazakhstan after experiencing a steep ballistic re-entry trajectory.

04-20.text: Danica Patrick wins the Indy Japan 300, becoming the first woman to win an IndyCar Series race.

04-21.text: This week in 2008, countdown clocks tick down across gaming forums for the launch of GTA IV.

04-22.text: Millions worldwide celebrate Earth Day with environmental rallies and tree-planting initiatives.

04-23.text: This week in 2008, reviews for Grand Theft Auto IV begin appearing, awarding the game near-perfect scores.

04-24.text: Canonical releases Ubuntu 8.04 LTS, code-named Hardy Heron, offering long-term support for desktops.

04-25.text: This week in 2008, video game retailers across North America and Europe stock shelves for GTA IV.

04-26.text: This week in 2008, Madonna releases her eleventh studio album, Hard Candy, in several European countries.

04-27.text: This week in 2008, fans form overnight queues outside game retailers to purchase Grand Theft Auto IV.

04-28.text: ISRO successfully launches ten satellites into orbit in a single mission using the PSLV-C9 rocket.

04-29.text: Rockstar Games releases Grand Theft Auto IV worldwide for PlayStation 3 and Xbox 360 to widespread acclaim.

04-30.text: Grand Theft Auto IV sells 3.6 million copies on its first day, shattering entertainment industry records.

05-01.text: This week in 2008, Grand Theft Auto IV generates over 310 million dollars in its first day of release.

05-02.text: Marvel Studios releases Iron Man in US theaters, launching the Marvel Cinematic Universe.

05-03.text: Microsoft officially withdraws its 47.5 billion dollar offer to acquire Yahoo! after talks stall.

05-04.text: Iron Man dominates the global box office, earning over 100 million dollars in its US opening weekend.

05-05.text: This week in 2008, Rockstar Games announces Grand Theft Auto IV surpassed 500 million dollars in week-one sales.

05-06.text: Barack Obama wins the North Carolina primary, taking a commanding lead in the Democratic delegate race.

05-07.text: Dmitry Medvedev is inaugurated as President of Russia at the Grand Kremlin Palace in Moscow.

05-08.text: The Olympic torch reaches the summit of Mount Everest for the first time in Olympic history.

05-09.text: The Wachowskis release their live-action adaptation of Speed Racer in theaters worldwide.

05-10.text: This week in 2008, Nintendo Wii consoles continue to face massive retail shortages worldwide.

05-11.text: This week in 2008, Coldplay's single 'Viva la Vida' enters music charts worldwide ahead of their album launch.

05-12.text: A powerful magnitude 7.9 earthquake strikes Sichuan province in southwest China.

05-13.text: Hewlett-Packard agrees to acquire IT services firm Electronic Data Systems for 13.9 billion dollars.

05-14.text: Zenit Saint Petersburg defeats Rangers 2-0 in Manchester to win the UEFA Cup.

05-15.text: The California Supreme Court rules that same-sex couples have a constitutional right to marry.

05-16.text: Disney releases The Chronicles of Narnia: Prince Caspian in North American movie theaters.
05-16.src: The Chronicles of Narnia: Prince Caspian (film)

05-17.text: Portsmouth defeats Cardiff City 1-0 at Wembley Stadium to win the English FA Cup.

05-18.text: Russia defeats Canada 5-4 in overtime to win the 2008 IIHF World Championship in Quebec City.

05-19.text: This week in 2008, NASA prepares the Phoenix Mars Lander for its descent onto the Martian north pole.

05-20.text: Ma Ying-jeou is officially inaugurated as President of the Republic of China in Taiwan.

05-21.text: Manchester United defeats Chelsea on penalties in Moscow to win the UEFA Champions League.

05-22.text: Indiana Jones and the Kingdom of the Crystal Skull opens worldwide, marking Harrison Ford's return to the role.
05-22.src: Indiana Jones and the Kingdom of the Crystal Skull

05-23.text: Twelve South American nations sign the UNASUR Constitutive Treaty in Brasilia.

05-24.text: Russia's Dima Bilan wins the Eurovision Song Contest in Belgrade with the song 'Believe'.

05-25.text: NASA's Phoenix lander touches down on the Martian arctic plains to search for signs of water ice.

05-26.text: NASA's Phoenix lander transmits its first high-resolution images from the surface of Mars.

05-27.text: Microsoft previews Windows 7's new multitouch interface during the D6 tech conference.

05-28.text: Nepal's Constituent Assembly formally abolishes the monarchy, declaring the country a republic.

05-29.text: This week in 2008, developers examine early builds of Google's upcoming Android mobile operating system.

05-30.text: The film adaptation of Sex and the City opens in movie theaters, topping the North American box office.

05-31.text: Space Shuttle Discovery launches on mission STS-124 to deliver Japan's Kibo lab module to the ISS.

06-01.text: A massive fire breaks out on the backlot of Universal Studios Hollywood, destroying historic film sets.

06-02.text: Space Shuttle Discovery docks with the International Space Station to install Japan's Kibo laboratory module.

06-03.text: Barack Obama clinches enough delegates to secure the Democratic nomination for US President.

06-04.text: Asus unveils the Eee PC 900 and 1000 series netbooks powered by Intel Atom processors at Computex.

06-05.text: This week in 2008, tech manufacturers showcase ultra-portable netbooks at the Computex trade show in Taipei.

06-06.text: DreamWorks Animation releases Kung Fu Panda in theaters across North America.

06-07.text: UEFA Euro 2008 kicks off, co-hosted by Austria and Switzerland.

06-08.text: Rafael Nadal defeats Roger Federer to win his fourth consecutive French Open singles title.

06-09.text: Steve Jobs unveils the iPhone 3G and the App Store at Apple's WWDC in San Francisco.

06-10.text: This week in 2008, Apple introduces MobileMe, an early cloud synchronization suite for email, contacts, and calendar.

06-11.text: NASA launches the Fermi Gamma-ray Space Telescope into low Earth orbit aboard a Delta II rocket.

06-12.text: Konami releases Metal Gear Solid 4: Guns of the Patriots worldwide for the PlayStation 3.
06-12.src: Metal Gear Solid 4: Guns of the Patriots

06-13.text: Marvel Studios releases The Incredible Hulk in movie theaters across North America.

06-14.text: Expo 2008 opens in Zaragoza, Spain, focusing on water conservation and sustainable development.

06-15.text: Coldplay releases their fourth studio album, Viva la Vida or Death and All His Friends.
06-15.src: Viva la Vida or Death and All His Friends

06-16.text: Tiger Woods wins the US Open at Torrey Pines in a dramatic 19-hole playoff against Rocco Mediate.

06-17.text: Mozilla releases Firefox 3, setting a world record with over eight million downloads in 24 hours.
The Boston Celtics beat the Los Angeles Lakers 131-92 in Game 6 to win the 2008 NBA Championship.

06-18.text: This week in 2008, Boston celebrates the Celtics' 17th NBA title, won against the Los Angeles Lakers.

06-19.text: NASA confirms the presence of water ice on Mars after photographed ice chunks vaporize over eight days.

06-20.text: This week in 2008, Mozilla sets a Guinness World Record for the most downloaded software in 24 hours with Firefox 3.

06-21.text: This week in 2008, Coldplay's album Viva la Vida debuts at number one on the UK Albums Chart.
06-21.src: Viva la Vida or Death and All His Friends

06-22.text: Spain defeats Italy in a penalty shootout in the Euro 2008 quarter-finals, breaking a 74-year curse.

06-23.text: This week in 2008, Google releases early developer preview builds of the Android mobile operating system.

06-24.text: This week in 2008, tech enthusiasts eagerly anticipate the commercial rollout of the iPhone 3G.

06-25.text: Germany defeats Turkey 3-2 in a dramatic UEFA Euro 2008 semi-final in Basel.

06-26.text: The US Supreme Court rules in District of Columbia v. Heller that the Second Amendment protects individual gun ownership.

06-27.text: Pixar releases the animated science-fiction film WALL-E in North American movie theaters.

06-28.text: This week in 2008, Nintendo releases Super Smash Bros. Brawl across Europe for the Wii.

06-29.text: Spain defeats Germany 1-0 to win UEFA Euro 2008, securing their first major international trophy since 1964.

06-30.text: Microsoft officially ceases standard retail distribution of Windows XP to push adoption of Windows Vista.

07-01.text: France assumes the six-month rotating presidency of the Council of the European Union.
07-01.src: Presidency of the Council of the European Union

07-02.text: Colombian security forces rescue Íngrid Betancourt and 14 other hostages in Operation Jaque.

07-03.text: Sony updates PS3 system software, introducing in-game XMB access and the PlayStation Trophy system.

07-04.text: This week in 2008, long lines form outside retail stores globally ahead of the iPhone 3G launch.

07-05.text: Venus Williams defeats her sister Serena Williams to win her fifth Wimbledon women's singles title.

07-06.text: Rafael Nadal defeats Roger Federer in an epic five-set Wimbledon final widely praised as tennis history's best.

07-07.text: The 34th G8 summit opens in Toyako, Japan, focusing on climate change and surging global food prices.

07-08.text: This week in 2008, Apple releases iTunes 7.7, adding support for the iPhone 3G and the new App Store.

07-09.text: This week in 2008, software developers eagerly upload their mobile creations to the new Apple App Store.

07-10.text: Apple officially launches the App Store via iTunes, opening with approximately 500 mobile applications.

07-11.text: Apple releases the iPhone 3G and iPhone OS 2.0 simultaneously across twenty-one countries worldwide.

07-12.text: This week in 2008, Apple sells one million iPhone 3G devices during its global debut weekend.

07-13.text: Forty-three countries establish the Union for the Mediterranean during an international summit in Paris.

07-14.text: Microsoft unveils the New Xbox Experience dashboard and announces Final Fantasy XIII for Xbox 360 at E3.

07-15.text: Nintendo reveals the Wii MotionPlus accessory and Wii Music during its E3 press conference in Los Angeles.

07-16.text: This week in 2008, major video game studios showcase their upcoming holiday lineups at E3 in Los Angeles.

07-17.text: The E3 2008 Media and Business Summit concludes after major announcements by Microsoft, Nintendo, and Sony.

07-18.text: Christopher Nolan's superhero film The Dark Knight opens in US theaters to universal critical acclaim.

07-19.text: This week in 2008, The Dark Knight sets a US single-day box office record of over 67 million dollars.

07-20.text: The Dark Knight sets a new all-time opening weekend box office record, earning 158.4 million dollars.

07-21.text: Former Bosnian Serb leader Radovan Karadzic is arrested in Belgrade after 13 years on the run.

07-22.text: This week in 2008, Heath Ledger's portrayal of the Joker in The Dark Knight draws worldwide acclaim.

07-23.text: Google launches Knol, an online user-written reference encyclopedia designed to compete with Wikipedia.

07-24.text: Barack Obama speaks before an estimated crowd of 200,000 people at the Victory Column in Berlin.

07-25.text: The comedy film Step Brothers, starring Will Ferrell and John C. Reilly, opens in North American theaters.

07-26.text: This week in 2008, Beijing opens three new subway lines and an airport express link ahead of the Olympics.

07-27.text: Spanish cyclist Carlos Sastre wins the 2008 Tour de France after holding off rivals in the final stages.

07-28.text: This week in 2008, anticipation builds for Microsoft's inaugural Summer of Arcade program on Xbox 360.

07-29.text: The US House of Representatives passes an official resolution apologizing for slavery and Jim Crow laws.

07-30.text: World Trade Organization negotiations on the Doha Development Round collapse in Geneva without agreement.

07-31.text: NASA scientists confirm the presence of water ice on Mars after the Phoenix lander analyzes a soil sample.

08-01.text: A total solar eclipse darkens skies across northern Canada, Greenland, Russia, and China.

08-02.text: This week in 2008, thousands of international athletes arrive in Beijing as the Olympic Village opens.

08-03.text: This week in 2008, Microsoft launches its first Summer of Arcade promotion on Xbox Live Arcade.

08-04.text: This week in 2008, Sony announces it has sold more than 20 million PlayStation Portable systems worldwide.

08-05.text: This week in 2008, CERN prepares the final cool-down phase of the Large Hadron Collider in Switzerland.

08-06.text: Jonathan Blow's acclaimed puzzle-platformer Braid launches on Xbox Live Arcade.

08-07.text: Armed conflict erupts in South Ossetia, initiating the Russo-Georgian War.

08-08.text: The 2008 Summer Olympics officially open in Beijing with a grand ceremony at the Bird's Nest stadium.

08-09.text: Czech shooter Katerina Emmons wins the first gold medal of the Beijing 2008 Olympic Games.

08-10.text: Michael Phelps wins the 400m individual medley in Beijing, breaking the world record.

08-11.text: Abhinav Bindra wins the men's 10m air rifle in Beijing, earning India's first individual Olympic gold medal.

08-12.text: French President Nicolas Sarkozy brokers a ceasefire agreement to end the Russo-Georgian War.

08-13.text: Michael Phelps wins his 10th and 11th career Olympic gold medals, setting an all-time record.

08-14.text: The US and Poland sign an agreement to place an American missile defense base on Polish soil.
08-14.src: US missile defense complex in Poland

08-15.text: The action-comedy Tropic Thunder, directed by Ben Stiller, opens in North American movie theaters.

08-16.text: Usain Bolt breaks the 100-meter world record with a time of 9.69 seconds at the Beijing Olympics.

08-17.text: Michael Phelps wins his eighth gold medal in Beijing, breaking Mark Spitz's single-Games record.

08-18.text: Pervez Musharraf resigns as President of Pakistan under threat of impeachment.

08-19.text: This week in 2008, Usain Bolt captivates the world with his iconic victory celebration in Beijing.

08-20.text: Usain Bolt breaks the 200-meter world record with a time of 19.30 seconds at the Beijing Olympics.

08-21.text: This week in 2008, the Beijing Olympics enter their final days, with the Bird's Nest full every night.

08-22.text: The Jamaican men's 4x100m relay team breaks the world record at the Beijing Olympic Games.

08-23.text: Joe Biden is formally announced as Barack Obama's vice presidential running mate.

08-24.text: The 2008 Summer Olympics conclude in Beijing with a grand closing ceremony at the National Stadium.

08-25.text: The Democratic National Convention opens at the Pepsi Center in Denver, Colorado.

08-26.text: Russia officially recognizes the independence of breakaway Georgian regions Abkhazia and South Ossetia.
08-26.src: International recognition of Abkhazia and South Ossetia

08-27.text: Barack Obama becomes the first African-American presidential nominee of a major US political party.

08-28.text: Barack Obama accepts the Democratic presidential nomination before 84,000 people in Denver.

08-29.text: John McCain selects Alaska Governor Sarah Palin as his vice presidential running mate.

08-30.text: This week in 2008, Google gets ready to unveil Chrome, its first web browser.

08-31.text: This week in 2008, anticipation builds as Google prepares to officially unveil its open-source browser, Chrome.

09-01.text: Google announces its new open-source web browser, Google Chrome, by distributing an introductory comic book.

09-02.text: Google releases the first beta version of its Google Chrome web browser for Windows.

09-03.text: Sarah Palin delivers her vice presidential acceptance speech at the Republican National Convention.

09-04.text: John McCain formally accepts the Republican presidential nomination at the convention in Saint Paul.

09-05.text: The European Space Agency's Rosetta probe performs a successful flyby of asteroid 2867 Steins.

09-06.text: Asif Ali Zardari is elected President of Pakistan by the country's electoral college.

09-07.text: The US government places mortgage giants Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac into federal conservatorship.
09-07.src: Federal takeover of Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac

09-08.text: Roger Federer defeats Andy Murray in straight sets to win his fifth consecutive US Open title.

09-09.text: Apple introduces the fourth-generation iPod nano and the second-generation iPod touch in San Francisco.

09-10.text: Physicists successfully circulate the first proton beam through the 27-kilometer Large Hadron Collider at CERN.

09-11.text: This week in 2008, CERN celebrates the successful initial beam test of the Large Hadron Collider.

09-12.text: Metallica releases Death Magnetic, their ninth studio album and their first in five years.

09-13.text: Hurricane Ike makes landfall near Galveston, Texas, causing widespread coastal flooding and power outages.

09-14.text: Sebastian Vettel wins the Italian Grand Prix, becoming the youngest driver to win a Formula 1 race.

09-15.text: Investment banking firm Lehman Brothers files for bankruptcy, sparking an escalation in the global financial crisis.

09-16.text: The US Federal Reserve authorizes an 85 billion dollar emergency loan to rescue insurer AIG from collapse.

09-17.text: The International Astronomical Union officially classifies Haumea as the solar system's fifth dwarf planet.

09-18.text: This week in 2008, stock markets worldwide suffer extreme turbulence following the collapse of Lehman Brothers.

09-19.text: The Large Hadron Collider suffers an electrical fault that causes a liquid helium leak, forcing a shutdown.

09-20.text: This week in 2008, Will Wright's evolutionary simulator Spore tops PC video game sales charts globally.

09-21.text: South African President Thabo Mbeki announces his formal resignation following a recall by his political party.

09-22.text: This week in 2008, tech blogs buzz with anticipation for the official unveiling of the first Android phone.

09-23.text: Google and T-Mobile unveil the T-Mobile G1, the first commercially released smartphone running the Android OS.

09-24.text: This week in 2008, Google releases the Android 1.0 Software Development Kit to developers worldwide.

09-25.text: Federal regulators seize Washington Mutual in what becomes the largest bank failure in United States history.

09-26.text: Barack Obama and John McCain meet in Mississippi for the first presidential debate of the 2008 campaign.

09-27.text: Astronaut Zhai Zhigang performs China's first extravehicular spacewalk during the Shenzhou 7 mission.

09-28.text: SpaceX's Falcon 1 rocket reaches orbit on its fourth launch, becoming the first privately built liquid-fueled craft to do so.

09-29.text: The US House of Representatives rejects the initial bailout bill, triggering a historic 777-point drop in the Dow.

09-30.text: This week in 2008, global credit markets freeze as banking turmoil spreads across European institutions.

10-01.text: Matsushita Electric Industrial officially changes its corporate name to Panasonic Corporation.

10-02.text: Joe Biden and Sarah Palin participate in the 2008 US vice presidential debate in Saint Louis.

10-03.text: President George W. Bush signs the 700 billion dollar Emergency Economic Stabilization Act into law.

10-04.text: This week in 2008, global markets react to the passage of the historic 700 billion dollar US bank bailout.

10-05.text: This week in 2008, European governments coordinate emergency measures to protect their commercial banks.

10-06.text: NASA's MESSENGER spacecraft completes its second close flyby of Mercury, mapping more of its surface.

10-07.text: Spotify officially launches its music streaming service by invitation in selected European countries.

10-08.text: The British government announces a 500 billion pound rescue package to stabilize the UK banking system.

10-09.text: This week in 2008, Spotify introduces its ad-supported streaming model to listeners in Europe.

10-10.text: Global stock markets plunge, capping the worst single-week decline for Wall Street in 75 years.

10-11.text: This week in 2008, EA prepares to launch Dead Space, a new sci-fi survival horror game.

10-12.text: Game designer Richard Garriott launches to the International Space Station aboard Soyuz TMA-13.

10-13.text: American economist Paul Krugman wins the Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences.

10-14.text: Apple unveils new MacBook and MacBook Pro notebooks crafted from a single block of aluminum.

10-15.text: Barack Obama and John McCain meet at Hofstra University for the third and final presidential debate.

10-16.text: This week in 2008, Apple begins selling its precision-crafted unibody aluminum MacBook notebooks.

10-17.text: This week in 2008, Electronic Arts releases Dead Space, earning acclaim for its atmospheric sci-fi horror.

10-18.text: This week in 2008, anticipation builds for the US arrival of HTC's Dream, the first Android phone.

10-19.text: Former US Secretary of State Colin Powell endorses Barack Obama for president on Meet the Press.

10-20.text: AC/DC releases Black Ice, their first studio album in eight years, debuting at number one worldwide.

10-21.text: CERN officially inaugurates the Large Hadron Collider with an international ceremony in Geneva.

10-22.text: India successfully launches Chandrayaan-1, its first uncrewed lunar probe, aboard a PSLV rocket.

10-23.text: The T-Mobile G1 goes on sale in the US, becoming the first commercially available Android phone.

10-24.text: Lionhead Studios releases the action role-playing game Fable II for the Xbox 360 in Europe.

10-25.text: This week in 2008, early Android adopters explore the newly launched Android Market on the T-Mobile G1.

10-26.text: This week in 2008, gamers dive into the open wasteland of Fallout 3 ahead of its global release.

10-27.text: Media Molecule releases LittleBigPlanet for the PlayStation 3, pioneering user-generated content.

10-28.text: Bethesda Softworks releases Fallout 3 in North America, redefining the post-apocalyptic RPG series.

10-29.text: Delta Air Lines and Northwest Airlines merge to create the world's largest commercial airline.

10-30.text: This week in 2008, Fallout 3 launches in Europe, winning critical praise for its vast Capital Wasteland.

10-31.text: Satoshi Nakamoto publishes the Bitcoin whitepaper, outlining a peer-to-peer electronic cash system.

11-01.text: Nintendo releases the Nintendo DSi handheld console in Japan, featuring dual cameras and internal storage.

11-02.text: Lewis Hamilton wins his first Formula One World Championship at the Brazilian Grand Prix on the final lap.

11-03.text: This week in 2008, anticipation builds worldwide on the eve of the historic United States presidential election.

11-04.text: Barack Obama is elected the 44th President of the United States, becoming the first African American president.

11-05.text: Newspapers sell out across the US as readers look for copies reporting Barack Obama's election win.

11-06.text: This week in 2008, gamers line up for midnight launches of Epic Games' tactical shooter Gears of War 2.

11-07.text: Epic Games and Microsoft release Gears of War 2 worldwide, exclusively for the Xbox 360 console.

11-08.text: India's Chandrayaan-1 spacecraft successfully enters lunar orbit, marking the nation's arrival at the Moon.

11-09.text: This week in 2008, Gears of War 2 sells over two million copies in its first weekend of release.

11-10.text: NASA declares the Phoenix Mars Lander mission officially ended after losing communications during Martian winter.

11-11.text: DICE and Electronic Arts release the first-person parkour action game Mirror's Edge for consoles.

11-12.text: This week in 2008, Mirror's Edge introduces gamers to fluid first-person momentum and parkour traversal.

11-13.text: This week in 2008, anticipation builds for Microsoft's major 'New Xbox Experience' dashboard overhaul.

11-14.text: India's Moon Impact Probe detaches from Chandrayaan-1 and successfully impacts the lunar south pole.

11-15.text: Space Shuttle Endeavour launches on mission STS-126 to expand the International Space Station's crew quarters.

11-16.text: Space Shuttle Endeavour successfully docks with the International Space Station on mission STS-126.

11-17.text: This week in 2008, Valve releases demo builds of Left 4 Dead, sparking viral multiplayer excitement.

11-18.text: Valve releases the cooperative survival horror shooter Left 4 Dead for PC and Xbox 360.

11-19.text: Microsoft rolls out the New Xbox Experience for Xbox 360, introducing customizable 3D Avatars.

11-20.text: This week in 2008, millions of Xbox 360 players design their new digital Avatars on Xbox Live.

11-21.text: The romantic fantasy film Twilight opens in theaters across North America, launching a global franchise.

11-22.text: This week in 2008, Twilight tops the box office, grossing nearly 70 million dollars in its opening weekend.

11-23.text: Guns N' Roses releases Chinese Democracy, their first album of original material in seventeen years.

11-24.text: This week in 2008, fans finally get Guns N' Roses' Chinese Democracy after years of delays.

11-25.text: Kanye West releases his influential synth-heavy album 808s & Heartbreak, popularizing Auto-Tune in pop music.

11-26.text: This week in 2008, gamers dive into Left 4 Dead's intense four-player cooperative zombie campaigns.

11-27.text: This week in 2008, shoppers across the United States gear up for Black Friday deals amid economic uncertainty.

11-28.text: This week in 2008, Nintendo reports massive sales for the newly launched DSi handheld across Japan.

11-29.text: This week in 2008, Space Shuttle Endeavour undocks from the ISS after delivering water recycling equipment.

11-30.text: Space Shuttle Endeavour lands safely at Edwards Air Force Base in California, concluding mission STS-126.

12-01.text: Barack Obama nominates former rival Hillary Clinton to serve as US Secretary of State.

12-02.text: Rockstar Games releases Grand Theft Auto IV for PC in North America.

12-03.text: This week in 2008, PC gamers explore the newly released Windows port of Grand Theft Auto IV.

12-04.text: This week in 2008, gamers test custom video editor tools in the newly released PC edition of GTA IV.

12-05.text: Honda announces its immediate withdrawal from Formula One racing due to the global economic crisis.

12-06.text: This week in 2008, tech fans anticipate the release of PlayStation Home, Sony's 3D social platform.

12-07.text: This week in 2008, Google prepares to take its Chrome browser out of beta, about 100 days after launch.

12-08.text: This week in 2008, Google Chrome approaches the milestone of exiting its initial beta phase.

12-09.text: Illinois Governor Rod Blagojevich is arrested by federal agents on public corruption charges.

12-10.text: The Channel Island of Sark holds its first democratic election, ending centuries of feudal rule.

12-11.text: Wall Street financier Bernard Madoff is arrested and charged with orchestrating a massive Ponzi scheme.

12-12.text: Switzerland officially joins the Schengen Area, abolishing land border checks with European neighbors.

12-13.text: This week in 2008, Sony launches the open beta of PlayStation Home, a 3D virtual world for the PS3.

12-14.text: An Iraqi journalist throws both of his shoes at US President George W. Bush during a press conference.

12-15.text: This week in 2008, viral videos of the shoe-throwing incident in Iraq circulate across the internet.

12-16.text: The US Federal Reserve slashes its target interest rate to near zero for the first time in history.

12-17.text: Time magazine names US President-elect Barack Obama as its Person of the Year.

12-18.text: This week in 2008, millions of PlayStation 3 owners explore the new virtual spaces of PlayStation Home.

12-19.text: The US government approves a 17.4 billion dollar emergency loan to rescue automakers GM and Chrysler.
12-19.src: Effects of the 2008–2010 automotive industry crisis on the United States

12-20.text: This week in 2008, the comedy film Yes Man, starring Jim Carrey, opens in theaters across North America.

12-21.text: Manchester United defeats LDU Quito 1-0 in Yokohama, Japan, to win the FIFA Club World Cup.

12-22.text: A massive coal ash containment failure in Tennessee releases over one billion gallons of ash slurry.
12-22.src: Kingston Fossil Plant coal fly ash slurry spill

12-23.text: Military officers seize power in Guinea in a bloodless coup following the death of President Lansana Conté.

12-24.text: This week in 2008, Nintendo Wii consoles remain one of the most sought-after holiday gifts worldwide.
12-24.src: Seventh generation of video game consoles

12-25.text: The family comedy-drama film Marley & Me opens in theaters, setting a Christmas Day box office record.

12-26.text: This week in 2008, post-holiday shoppers crowd electronics retailers seeking discounted netbooks.

12-27.text: This week in 2008, Apple prepares to remove digital rights management restrictions from iTunes music.

12-28.text: This week in 2008, David Fincher's The Curious Case of Benjamin Button opens to strong reviews.
12-28.src: The Curious Case of Benjamin Button (film)

12-29.text: This week in 2008, tech analysts highlight the explosive popularity of netbooks during holiday sales.

12-30.text: This week in 2008, Lil Wayne's Tha Carter III finishes the year as the best-selling album in the US.

12-31.text: An extra leap second is added at the end of the year to synchronize atomic clocks with Earth's rotation.

facts.text: The iPhone 3G launched in July 2008 at a subsidized starting price of 199 dollars in the United States.
Apple's App Store launched in 2008 with only around 500 applications available for download.
Netbooks like the Asus Eee PC surged in popularity in 2008 due to their small size and low cost.
Facebook surpassed MySpace in total worldwide monthly unique visitors for the first time in 2008.
The original HTC Dream featured a physical slide-out QWERTY keyboard alongside its touchscreen.
Windows XP retained over 70 percent of global desktop operating system market share throughout 2008.
Windows Vista struggled with adoption in 2008 due to steep hardware requirements and driver issues.
The original MacBook Air sold for 1,799 dollars and lacked an optical drive and Ethernet port.
In 2008, Twitter had a strict 140-character limit modeled after standard SMS text messaging.
A 16 GB USB flash drive cost around 50 to 70 dollars in retail stores in 2008.
The Nintendo Wii was the best-selling video game console worldwide throughout 2008.
Sony introduced Trophies on the PlayStation 3 in 2008 to rival Xbox 360 Achievements.
Xbox Live introduced customizable 3D Avatars with the New Xbox Experience update in 2008.
In 2008, standard definition CRT televisions were still widespread in homes despite LCD adoption.
Grand Theft Auto IV set entertainment records in 2008 by generating 310 million dollars on day one.
Guitar Hero and Rock Band plastic instrument controllers peaked in cultural popularity during 2008.
The Nokia N95 and Nokia E71 were among the top executive smartphones worldwide in 2008.
BlackBerry devices dominated the business mobile market in 2008 thanks to BBM and physical keyboards.
Apple's iPhone OS 2.0 introduced native third-party apps and Microsoft Exchange support.
In 2008, a Netflix subscription primarily meant receiving physical DVDs in the mail via red envelopes.
Hulu launched publicly in 2008, offering free ad-supported streaming of television shows.
Blu-ray officially won the high-definition optical disc format war over HD DVD in early 2008.
A standalone Blu-ray player typically cost between 300 and 400 dollars in 2008.
The PlayStation 3 was widely praised as one of the most affordable and upgradeable Blu-ray players in 2008.
In 2008, Google Chrome introduced an isolated multi-process tab architecture to prevent browser crashes.
The Intel Core 2 Duo and Core 2 Quad were the dominant desktop processors in 2008.
Intel introduced the Nehalem microarchitecture and the Core i7 processor branding in late 2008.
Nvidia launched the GeForce GTX 280 and GTX 260 graphics cards in mid-2008.
ATI released the Radeon HD 4870 in 2008, the first graphics card to feature GDDR5 memory.
The standard PC monitor resolution for desktop gaming in 2008 was 1280x1024 or 1680x1050.
A mainstream laptop hard drive typically offered between 160 GB and 250 GB of storage in 2008.
Early consumer solid-state drives in 2008 cost several hundred dollars for merely 32 GB or 64 GB.
Spore allowed players to design creatures, vehicles, and buildings that uploaded to a shared online Sporepedia.
Left 4 Dead popularized four-player cooperative zombie survival gameplay when released in late 2008.
Bethesda transitioned the Fallout series to full 3D real-time gameplay with Fallout 3 in 2008.
Super Smash Bros. Brawl introduced third-party guest characters Solid Snake and Sonic the Hedgehog.
Metal Gear Solid 4 required multi-gigabyte chapter installations on the PlayStation 3 hard drive in 2008.
facts.src: Metal Gear Solid 4: Guns of the Patriots

facts.text: World of Warcraft reached 11 million active subscribers following the release of Wrath of the Lich King.
facts.src: World of Warcraft: Wrath of the Lich King

facts.text: Wrath of the Lich King sold 2.8 million copies in its first 24 hours, setting a PC gaming sales record.
facts.src: World of Warcraft: Wrath of the Lich King

facts.text: Dead Space debuted in 2008 with a diegetic user interface that integrated health and ammo directly into the character.
Braid helped spark the modern indie game movement when it released on Xbox Live Arcade in August 2008.
Castle Crashers became a standout indie hit on Xbox Live Arcade during the 2008 Summer of Arcade.
LittleBigPlanet introduced the tagline 'Play, Create, Share', empowering players to build and publish custom levels.
Mirror's Edge introduced an innovative first-person parkour mechanic and a stark minimalist art style.
The Dark Knight became the highest-grossing film of 2008, earning over one billion dollars worldwide.
Iron Man launched Marvel Studios' cinematic universe and grossed over 585 million dollars globally in 2008.
Heath Ledger received widespread posthumous praise for his performance as the Joker in The Dark Knight.
Pixar's WALL-E earned universal critical acclaim in 2008 for its largely dialogue-free opening half.
Twilight sparked a massive cultural phenomenon among young adults upon its theatrical release in late 2008.
Coldplay's 'Viva la Vida' topped music charts across several continents in 2008.
Katy Perry scored her breakthrough in 2008 with the pop album One of the Boys.
Lady Gaga released her debut album The Fame in 2008, featuring international hits 'Just Dance' and 'Poker Face'.
Kanye West's 808s & Heartbreak popularized emotive Auto-Tune vocals and Roland TR-808 drum patterns in hip-hop.
Lil Wayne's album Tha Carter III sold over one million copies in its first week in the United States in 2008.
The Rickroll meme became a global phenomenon on April Fools' Day in 2008 after YouTube linked all featured videos to it.
The LOLcats internet meme and the website 'I Can Has Cheezburger?' reached mainstream popularity in 2008.
Flash games hosted on websites like Newgrounds, Kongregate, and Armor Games were a daily pastime for gamers in 2008.
MSN Messenger and Windows Live Messenger were among the most popular instant messaging services in 2008.
AIM was still a primary communication tool for millions of teenagers and young adults across North America in 2008.
Skype was the primary application used for peer-to-peer voice and video calls on personal computers in 2008.
In 2008, Apple charged a 99 dollar annual fee for MobileMe, which suffered frequent server outages at launch.
The price of oil peaked at an all-time record of over 147 dollars per barrel in July 2008.
In 2008, US average gasoline prices exceeded 4 dollars per gallon for the first time in history.
The Large Hadron Collider at CERN was successfully turned on in September 2008 before suffering a helium leak.
NASA's Phoenix lander confirmed the presence of water ice on Mars during its Arctic surface mission in 2008.
The open-source Chromium project was launched in September 2008 alongside the initial release of Google Chrome.
Spotify launched in late 2008 as an invitation-only desktop service offering legal on-demand music streaming.
BitTorrent client uTorrent was celebrated for its tiny file size of less than 300 kilobytes throughout 2008.
Limewire and Frostwire were still widely used peer-to-peer file-sharing programs among computer users in 2008.
Winamp remained a popular MP3 music player software on Windows PCs throughout 2008.
In 2008, standard songs purchased on the iTunes Store were priced at 99 cents each.
The Amazon Kindle, released in late 2007, remained frequently out of stock throughout most of 2008.
Nintendo DSi eliminated the Game Boy Advance cartridge slot found on previous DS models when revealed in 2008.
Sony launched PlayStation Home in late 2008 as a virtual 3D community hub for PlayStation 3 users.
Satoshi Nakamoto published the Bitcoin whitepaper in October 2008, proposing decentralized digital money.
Grand Theft Auto IV featured around twenty in-game radio stations playing over two hundred licensed tracks.
Nintendo released Wii Fit with the Wii Balance Board in 2008, popularizing active video games.
Super Smash Bros. Brawl included a story mode called The Subspace Emissary with full CGI cutscenes.
Spore sparked user protests in 2008 over its restrictive SecuROM digital rights management software.
Fallout 3 introduced the Vault-Tec Assisted Targeting System, pausing gameplay for tactical targeting.
Gears of War 2 popularized wave-based cooperative survival with its influential Horde mode in 2008.
Fable II introduced an AI dog companion that helped players find buried treasure and fought enemies.
Mirror's Edge used bright red visual highlights called Runner Vision to suggest routes through levels.
Braid featured a universal time-rewind mechanic that let players undo any mistake instantly.
Capcom released Mega Man 9 in 2008, deliberately returning to retro 8-bit NES graphics and audio.
Star Wars: The Force Unleashed showcased advanced physics and digital molecular matter simulation.
Professor Layton and the Curious Village made its Western debut on the Nintendo DS in 2008.
facts.src: Professor Layton and the Curious Village

facts.text: Atlus released Persona 4 for the PlayStation 2 in 2008, earning acclaim for its murder mystery plot.
Sega released Valkyria Chronicles in 2008, blending tactical role-playing with a watercolor aesthetic.
Goichi Suda released No More Heroes for the Wii in 2008, featuring motion-controlled beam katana duels.
Capcom released Super Street Fighter II Turbo HD Remix in 2008, featuring redrawn 1080p graphics.
facts.src: Super Street Fighter II Turbo HD Remix

facts.text: Nintendo announced the Wii MotionPlus accessory in 2008 to provide true one-to-one motion tracking.
Xbox 360 owners in 2008 still feared the Red Ring of Death, covered by a three-year warranty.
Sony released the rumble-enabled DualShock 3 controller in North America and Europe in spring 2008.
The App Store established 99 cents as the defining price point for mobile video games and utilities.
Sega's Super Monkey Ball was a flagship launch game demonstrating tilt controls on the iPhone 3G.
Tap Tap Revenge became one of the most downloaded early rhythm games on the Apple App Store in 2008.
Typical netbooks in 2008 featured small 7-inch to 10-inch displays and cramped compact keyboards.
The Intel Atom N270 processor powered the vast majority of consumer netbooks released in 2008.
Acer released the Aspire One netbook in 2008, quickly becoming one of the best-selling models.
The USB 3.0 specification was officially finalized in November 2008, introducing SuperSpeed transfers.
DDR3 SDRAM began replacing DDR2 as standard system memory on high-end desktop motherboards in 2008.
Nvidia launched the GeForce 9800 GTX graphics card in April 2008 for desktop gaming rigs.
Crytek released Crysis Warhead in 2008, optimized to run better than the demanding original Crysis.
Valve began releasing major class-specific content updates for Team Fortress 2 throughout 2008.
Valve announced Steam Cloud in 2008, allowing players to save game data automatically to remote servers.
Good Old Games launched in public beta in 2008, offering classic PC games without digital copyright DRM.
Spotify launched offering music streaming at 160 kbps using the Ogg Vorbis audio compression codec.
SoundCloud launched publicly in October 2008, allowing musicians to share audio files with wave visualizers.
AirBed & Breakfast, later known as Airbnb, was officially founded in San Francisco in August 2008.
Dropbox officially launched to the public in September 2008, offering simple cloud file synchronization.
Stack Overflow was launched in 2008 as an open question-and-answer website for software developers.
GitHub was officially launched in April 2008, transforming open-source Git repository hosting.
Google Street View expanded outside the United States for the first time in 2008, adding French cities.
The English Wikipedia passed two and a half million articles in 2008.
Internet Explorer was used by over 60 percent of web surfers in 2008, though Firefox was rising fast.
Adobe released Flash Player 10 in 2008, introducing GPU hardware acceleration and new 3D visual effects.
YouTube began testing 720p high-definition video playback for the first time in late 2008.
YouTube switched its standard desktop video player aspect ratio from 4:3 to 16:9 widescreen in 2008.
Standard DVD discs remained the overwhelmingly dominant home video format in 2008, outpacing Blu-ray.
Blockbuster still operated thousands of physical video rental stores across North America in 2008.
Roku released its first set-top box in 2008, made to stream Netflix to the TV.
Apple introduced a major software update in 2008 that let Apple TV rent movies directly without a computer.
The post-credits scene in Iron Man surprised 2008 moviegoers by teasing the future Avengers Initiative.
Slumdog Millionaire premiered at fall film festivals in 2008, quickly becoming an international hit.
The musical film Mamma Mia! became the highest-grossing film of all time at the UK box office in 2008.
Radiohead released the physical CD version of In Rainbows in early 2008 following its pay-what-you-want debut.
Indie folk band Fleet Foxes released their acclaimed self-titled debut album in June 2008.
MGMT's debut album spawned global indie electro-pop hits 'Kids' and 'Time to Pretend' in 2008.
Welsh singer Duffy had the best-selling album in the United Kingdom in 2008 with Rockferry.
Suzanne Collins published The Hunger Games in September 2008, launching a bestselling book trilogy.
The first season of Breaking Bad aired on AMC in early 2008, starring Bryan Cranston as Walter White.
The acclaimed time-travel episode 'The Constant' from Lost season 4 aired on ABC in February 2008.
Mad Men won the Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Drama Series in 2008, a first for basic cable AMC.
The animated film and television series Star Wars: The Clone Wars premiered in theaters and on TV in 2008.
Usain Bolt ran his historic 9.69-second 100-meter world record sprint in 2008 with an untied shoelace.
Swimmers broke dozens of world records at the 2008 Olympics wearing Speedo's polyurethane LZR Racer suit.
The National Aquatics Center, known as the Water Cube, hosted Olympic swimming events in Beijing in 2008.
Cristiano Ronaldo won his first Ballon d'Or award in 2008 after leading Manchester United to European glory.
SpaceX's fourth launch of Falcon 1 in 2008 proved that private aerospace companies could reach orbit.
Virgin Galactic unveiled the design of SpaceShipTwo and its White Knight Two carrier aircraft in 2008.
Tesla delivered the first production units of the all-electric Tesla Roadster sports car in 2008.
Shepard Fairey's stylized 'Hope' portrait of Barack Obama became an iconic cultural image in 2008.
Craigslist was the dominant online classified advertisements website for housing and sales in 2008.
Social news aggregator Digg reached peak web traffic in 2008 before facing rising competition from Reddit.
Internet forums drove viral web phenomena like Rickrolling in 2008.
Pocket-sized Flip Video camcorders were among the most popular consumer tech gadgets of 2008.
Sony and Apple competed intensely in 2008 with compact flash-based Walkman and iPod MP3 players.
